breakfast.name: Fried Breadfruit with Fish
instructions: Fry breadfruit slices
Season and fry fish
Serve together

breakfast.name: Banana Porridge
instructions: Mash bananas, cook with coconut milk
Add sugar and cinnamon

breakfast.name: Papaya with Lime and Coconut
instructions: Papaya grows abundantly on the São Tomé islands
The volcanic soil and equatorial climate produce exceptionally sweet fruit
Simply cut and dressed with lime juice and coconut
The lime juice cuts the sweetness of the ripe papaya
Fresh grated coconut adds texture and tropical richness
breakfast.description: São Tomé tropical papaya breakfast -- ripe papaya (grown in volcanic soil, equatorial sweet) dressed with fresh lime juice and fresh grated coconut. The volcanic soil and equatorial climate produce exceptional fruit. Lime cuts the sweetness.

breakfast.name: Tapioca with Coconut Milk
ingredients: Tapioca starch (from cassava -- grown on the islands)
instructions: Tapioca is made from cassava -- widely grown on São Tomé since Portuguese introduction
Cooked with coconut milk into a thick, silky pudding
The coconut trees grow throughout the islands -- coconut milk is a local product
Sweetened and served warm or cold as breakfast
breakfast.description: São Tomé tapioca porridge -- cassava-derived tapioca cooked in locally-produced coconut milk (coconut trees grow throughout the islands) with sugar and vanilla. Both cassava and coconut are island staples introduced under Portuguese colonization.

lunch.name: Calulú (Fish and Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Layer fish and vegetables in pot
Add palm oil and water
Simmer 45 min until thick
Serve with funje (corn porridge)
lunch.description: São Tomé's national dish — fish and vegetable stew in palm oil.

lunch.name: Funje (Corn Porridge)
instructions: Boil water
Stir in cornmeal until thick
Shape and serve with stew
lunch.description: Thick corn porridge — accompaniment to calulú.

lunch.name: Calulu de Peixe (Fish Stew)
ingredients: Fresh fish (sea bream, grouper, or any local catch)
Palm oil (the São Tomé essential fat)
instructions: Calulu de peixe is the signature São Tomé dish -- a rich fish stew
Palm oil is the foundation -- it gives the deep orange color and earthy flavor
São Tomé palm oil: the island produces its own red palm oil
The vegetables: okra and eggplant in the stew with the fish
A complex stew that takes time but is deeply satisfying
São Tomé cuisine is a blend of African and Portuguese influences
lunch.description: São Tomé signature fish stew -- fresh fish with okra and eggplant in a palm oil base (the island produces its own red palm oil) with tomatoes, garlic, and fresh herbs. The red palm oil gives the deep orange color and earthy richness. São Tomé cuisine blends African and Portuguese.

lunch.name: Muamba de Galinha (Chicken in Palm Oil)
instructions: Muamba de galinha is the São Tomé chicken dish -- deeply flavored with palm oil
The same dish exists in Angola and other Portuguese-speaking African countries
Palm oil: the mother sauce of central and West African cooking
The palm nuts are sometimes added for additional palm flavor
Okra thickens the sauce
The dish reflects the African-Portuguese colonial connection
lunch.description: São Tomé chicken in palm oil -- chicken pieces braised in red palm oil with garlic, onion, tomatoes, and okra. The same dish exists across Portuguese-speaking Africa (Angola, etc.). Palm oil is the mother sauce of central African cooking. Okra thickens. The African-Portuguese colonial connection on a plate.

lunch.name: Arroz com Coco (Coconut Rice)
instructions: Coconut rice is eaten throughout the African tropics and the Caribbean
São Tomé: coconut trees everywhere -- coconut milk is used in cooking throughout
The rice absorbs the coconut milk as it cooks
The result: slightly sweet, fragrant, creamy rice
Served alongside fish or chicken dishes
lunch.description: São Tomé coconut rice -- rice cooked in locally-produced coconut milk until creamy and fragrant. Coconut trees grow throughout the islands; coconut milk is used in cooking across São Tomé cuisine. Served alongside fish or chicken dishes.

dinner.name: Grilled Fish with Pilipili
ingredients: Pilipili sauce: chili, garlic, lemon, oil
instructions: Make pilipili sauce
Season fish, grill until flaky
Serve with pilipili
dinner.description: Grilled fish with fiery pilipili sauce.

dinner.name: Chicken Muamba
instructions: Brown chicken in palm oil
Add vegetables
Simmer 30 min
dinner.description: Chicken in palm oil sauce with okra.

dinner.name: Cachupa Rica Santomense (Hominy Stew)
ingredients: Chourico, smoked pork ribs, pig trotters
instructions: Cachupa is the national dish of Cape Verde -- but São Tomé has its own version
São Tomé was historically connected to Cape Verde under Portuguese administration
The São Tomé version (cachupa rica = rich cachupa) uses more meat
Dried hominy corn simmered for hours with smoked meats and legumes
The root vegetables and cabbage added toward the end
The richest version has a variety of smoked meats
dinner.description: São Tomé Portuguese-African corn stew -- dried hominy corn simmered for hours with smoked pork, chourico, and beans. Adapted from the Cape Verdean cachupa (the two islands were linked under Portuguese administration). The rica (rich) version includes more smoked meats and vegetables.

dinner.name: Grilled Lobster
instructions: São Tomé and Príncipe has some of the best lobster in the world
Spiny lobster (not the clawed European or Maine type) is found in the island waters
Grilled with garlic butter -- the simplest preparation for excellent ingredients
The lobster is split and grilled
The volcanic waters of the Atlantic surrounding the islands are cold enough for excellent seafood
dinner.description: São Tomé spiny lobster -- fresh Atlantic spiny lobster from São Tomé waters split and grilled with garlic butter and lemon. The pristine Atlantic waters around the volcanic islands produce exceptional seafood. Simple preparation for excellent ingredients.

dinner.name: Batata Doce Frita (Fried Sweet Potato)
instructions: Sweet potato grows well in São Tomé tropical soil
Simply fried until golden and crispy outside
A common side dish and snack throughout the islands
Often served alongside grilled fish or chicken
dinner.description: São Tomé fried sweet potato -- locally grown sweet potato fried until golden and crispy, served with hot pepper sauce. Grown in the tropical volcanic soil of São Tomé. A simple side and snack throughout the islands.

snacks.name: Banana Fritters
instructions: Mash bananas, mix with flour and sugar
Fry spoonfuls until golden

snacks.name: Banana Frita (Fried Plantain)
instructions: Fried plantain is eaten throughout tropical Africa and the Caribbean
São Tomé: plantains grow abundantly
Ripe (yellow) plantains: sweet when fried -- the Caribbean-style
Or green plantains: starchy and savory -- the West African style
Both styles are eaten in São Tomé
snacks.description: São Tomé fried plantain -- ripe yellow plantain fried until caramelized and sweet (Caribbean-style) or green plantain fried starchy and savory (West African-style). Both styles are eaten on the islands. Plantains grow abundantly in the tropical climate.

snacks.name: Chocolate from São Tomé
ingredients: São Tomé single-origin chocolate (Theobroma cacao -- forastero type, grown since Portuguese era)
instructions: São Tomé is one of the world great single-origin chocolate sources
Cacao was introduced by Portuguese colonizers in the 15th century
The island became a major cacao producer during colonialism
Today: single-origin São Tomé chocolate is internationally prized
The flavor: earthy, fruity, complex -- the volcanic soil contributes
The Claudio Corallo estate: one of the most famous São Tomé chocolate producers
snacks.description: São Tomé single-origin chocolate -- cacao introduced by Portuguese colonizers in the 15th century; the island became a major producer. Today São Tomé is internationally prized for complex, earthy, fruity single-origin chocolate. The volcanic soil contributes to the flavor. Claudio Corallo is one of the most celebrated estates.

snacks.name: Fruta do Pao (Breadfruit)
instructions: Breadfruit in São Tomé -- introduced by Portuguese from Pacific voyages
Roasted over fire: the exterior chars, the interior becomes soft and creamy
Fried in slices: becomes golden and slightly crispy
Eaten as a starch alongside fish or as a snack
snacks.description: São Tomé breadfruit -- introduced by Portuguese from Pacific voyages, now roasted over fire (charred exterior, creamy interior) or fried in slices. A starch eaten alongside fish or as a snack throughout the islands.

desserts.name: Chocolate Mousse
instructions: Melt chocolate
Whip cream and eggs separately
Fold together
Chill 2 hours
desserts.description: Made with São Tomé's world-renowned cocoa.

desserts.name: Banana com Chocolate (Banana with Chocolate)
ingredients: São Tomé chocolate (70% cacao or higher)
instructions: The combination of local banana and local chocolate
São Tomé produces both bananas and among the world best cacao
The ripe banana sliced alongside a piece of São Tomé chocolate
Or melted chocolate drizzled over the banana
The simplest and most local São Tomé dessert
desserts.description: São Tomé banana with local chocolate -- ripe banana alongside São Tomé single-origin chocolate (or melted over). Both are local products from the islands. The most simply local São Tomé dessert pairing.

desserts.name: Arroz Doce (Sweet Rice Pudding)
instructions: Arroz doce is the Portuguese sweet rice pudding -- present across the Lusophone world
São Tomé was a Portuguese colony until 1975 -- Portuguese food culture is embedded
The rice is cooked in milk until very thick and creamy
Egg yolks added for richness
Lemon zest is the essential aromatic
Cinnamon dusted on top -- the Portuguese dessert signature
desserts.description: São Tomé Portuguese sweet rice pudding -- short-grain rice cooked in milk until very thick and creamy with egg yolks, lemon zest, and vanilla, dusted with cinnamon. Portugal colonized São Tomé until 1975; Portuguese dessert tradition is embedded in the cuisine.

drinks.name: Palm Wine
instructions: Tap palm tree, collect sap
Serve fresh

drinks.name: Cacao Juice
instructions: Scoop pulp from cocoa pods
Mix with water and sugar
Strain
drinks.description: Juice from fresh cocoa fruit pulp.

drinks.name: Palm Wine (Vinho de Palma)
ingredients: Raffia palm sap (collected from the cut flower of the palm tree)
instructions: Palm wine is collected from the raffia palm tree
The palm is tapped at the flower -- the sap flows out
Fresh palm wine: slightly sweet, not yet very alcoholic
Fermented palm wine (a few days): increasingly alcoholic, sour
Very old palm wine: vinegary, strongly alcoholic
Collected and sold in gourds or bottles by palm wine tappers
The morning palm wine is fresh and sweet -- the evening version is more alcoholic
drinks.description: São Tomé palm wine -- sap collected from the tapped raffia palm flower, naturally fermenting over time. Fresh (morning): sweet, lightly alcoholic. Aged (days): more sour and stronger. The palm wine tapper climbs the palm daily to collect and sell by gourd or bottle.
